compounding_issues: Session 1-3 kept everything in a single app.py that grew to ~435 lines, forcing the session 4 repository-pattern refactor to claw back maintainability

Session 3 introduced Redis as a hard runtime dependency (Celery broker); session 5 compounded it by adding a Redis-backed Flask-Limiter storage, requiring fakeredis+lupa hacks in tests and an apt-get attempt to install redis-server
Migration debt built up across sessions: owner_id (session 2) then email column (session 3) were each added via non-destructive ALTER TABLE guards, growing init_db complexity
key_decisions: App-factory pattern (create_app) with injected database/jwt_secret/rate_limit — made every later session trivially testable with in-memory DBs
JWT auth with owner-scoped tasks and 404-on-foreign-tasks (session 2) — non-leaking ownership model that shaped all subsequent feature work
Non-destructive migration strategy in session 2 preserved existing databases and was cleanly extended in session 3
Celery async notification with env-overridable Redis config and a mock email task (session 3) kept infra optional
Repository pattern + dedicated db.py in session 4 removed all raw SQL from routes while keeping all 54 tests green without modification
Cursor-based pagination and shared-budget per-user rate limiting in session 5 as the cross-cutting layer on top of the refactored stack
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality improved steadily across all five sessions. Test coverage grew monotonically (20 -> 43 -> 54 -> 54 -> 76 tests, all passing at every commit), and architectural quality rose sharply at session 4, where the repository refactor cut app.py from ~435 lines to ~270 and eliminated raw SQL from route code without breaking a single existing test. Session 5 added genuinely production-grade cross-cutting concerns (429 responses with Retry-After, per-user rate budgets, cursor pagination) that sat cleanly on the repository layer. The only soft spot is a mounting infrastructure coupling to Redis that the agent papered over with fakeredis rather than addressing, and the greenfield-to-refactor arc suggests the early single-file approach deferred necessary structure until late.
story_review.summary: A textbook-quality incremental build: each session's changes sit naturally on the prior commit, the mid-story refactor is behavior-preserving and provably clean, and the final codebase is well-layered and thoroughly tested despite growing Redis coupling.
